sentences.text:
Opposite Party :- State of U.P.
Counsel for Applicant :- Vaibhav Shandilya,Sr. Advocate Counsel for Opposite Party :- G.A.,Dhirendra Singh Hon'ble Subhash Chandra Sharma,J.
Heard learned counsel for the applicant, learned counsel for the opposite party as well as learned A.G.A. for the State and perused the material placed on record.
This anticipatory bail application has been moved seeking anticipatory bail in Case Crime No. 484 of 2022, under sections 498A, 304B I.P.C. and 3/4D.P. Act, Police Station Kotwali, District Jhansi.
Facts in brief are that sister of the informant was wedded to the son of the present applicant on 16.01.2017.
She was taken to the district hospital then referred to medical college but she died on the way to the medical college on 12.09.2022.
As per allegations in F.I.R. there was demand of dowry on the part of applicant, his wife and son as a result she was subjected to harassment.
When her dead body was seen by the informant it appeared to him that it was blueish.
The inquest was conducted on the same day in presence of the informant and present F.I.R. was lodged after three months on 12.12.2022.
In post mortem cause of death could not be ascertained.

sentences.text: It is submitted by learned counsel for the applicant that he is innocent and have falsely been implicated in this case with false allegations of demand of dowry and harassment of the deceased.
It is also submitted that F.I.R. has been lodged after inordinate delay of three months from the date of death of the deceased.
Though the informant was present at the time of inquest of the deceased where no any such suspicion was disclosed by him.
It is further submitted that deceased and her husband both were teachers and attending their schools with the same vehicle.
There was no any dispute relating to demand of dowry between both of them and no any such complaint was made by the deceased prior to the alleged incident.
It is also submitted that the deceased was issueless and was being treated in the hospital.

Later on she was suffering from heart disease and on the date of her death her health was not good and there was uneasiness and sweating that was the reason she was taken to the district hospital where doctors attended her and provided the medicine Sorbitrate and other tablets and referred her to physician and also for E.C.G.
She was taken to medical college but on the way she died.

During post mortem no any external injury or symptom of poisoning was found but cause of the death could not be ascertained with doctors and till now there is no any report on record to show that she committed suicide or her death was caused otherwise than in normal course.
Lastly, it is submitted that applicant is under apprehension of imminent arrest.
In case, the applicant is released on bail, he would not misuse the liberty of bail and would cooperate with the investigation.

Learned counsel for the opposite party as well as learned A.G.A. opposed the prayer as aforesaid and urged that in this case there was demand of dowry and harassment of the deceased by the applicant and other members of his family.
When the informant saw the dead body of the deceased which appeared to be blueish but he guessed that her death was not in normal course.
It is also urged that the delay in lodging the F.I.R. was on account of mental upset of the informant.

On considering the facts and circumstances of the case, submissions made by learned counsel for both the parties as well as learned A.G.A. and perusal of record along with the medical treatment provided to the deceased and without expressing any opinion on the merits of the case and considering the nature of accusation and his antecedents, the applicant is entitled to be released on anticipatory bail in this case for the limited period considering the exception considered by the Hon'ble Supreme Court in the case of Sushila Aggarwal Vs. State (NCT of Delhi)-2020 SCC Online SC 98.

opennyai_summary.decision:
In the event of arrest of the applicant- Ram Bihari, shall be released on anticipatory bail till the submission of police report under Section 173 (2) Cr.P.C., on furnishing a personal bond of Rs.
25,000/- with two sureties each in the like amount to the satisfaction of the Station House Officer of the police station concerned with the following conditions:-
(i) The applicant shall make himself available for interrogation by a police office as and when required;
(ii) The applicant shall not directly or indirectly, make any inducement, threat or promise to any person acquainted with the facts of the case so as to dissuade from disclosing such facts to the Court or to any police office;
